housing: Dudley borough is part of the Black Country, with Victorian terraces built for its industries, large post-war council-built estates and inter-war suburbs such as Kingswinford and Halesowen. Stourbridge has more Victorian and Edwardian villas. Past mining and limestone workings under parts of the borough mean some homes have suffered subsidence, and canals run through many neighbourhoods.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces: photograph back yards, outhouses and any damp low on walls or in cellars.
Areas with past mining or limestone workings: photograph any cracks in walls, ceilings and around door frames so later movement can be compared.
Post-war estate homes: photograph fences, gates, sheds and garden condition, which are often disputed at check-out.
Flats near Brierley Hill and Merry Hill: photograph the communal entrance, bin store and parking bay, and count fobs and keys.
Canal-side homes: photograph gardens and boundaries near the water and any damp on low walls.
tenantHelp: Private tenants with disrepair or unsafe conditions can contact Dudley Council's private sector housing team.
